content.text:
I reproduced the crash deterministically (3/3 attempts). Here's the summary:

## Reproduction steps
1. Launch **BenchTarget** (`dev.lincforge.benchtarget`) on the Android phone.
2. From the home menu, tap **Catalog**.
3. Scroll to and tap **Item 013** (13th row in the catalog list).
4. App immediately crashes and dumps you back to the Android launcher/home screen — before the item-detail screen (with its **Export** button) ever finishes rendering.

This is 100% reproducible: I triggered it 3 separate times (fresh app launch each time). Items 001–012 and 014 all open their detail screens normally and the **Export** button works without issue on every one of them I tested (001–012). Only **Item 013** crashes, and it crashes on opening the item, not on the Export tap itself — it never gets far enough to show the Export button. The user's recollection of "crashes when exporting" is understandable since the item screen's only purpose is to export, but the actual trigger is opening that specific catalog entry.

## Exception class / message
I could **not** retrieve this. This session's toolset only gave me Maestro UI-automation (tap/inspect/screenshot/record) — there was no adb/logcat/shell access, and the device didn't surface an "App keeps stopping" dialog or crash notification (it silently died back to the launcher, which is typical of a fatal uncaught exception with crash dialogs suppressed). If you can grant logcat/adb access (or point me at a crash-reporting backend like a Linear/Sentry project this app reports to), I can pull the exact exception class and message.

## Additional evidence collected
- Screenshots of the Catalog list (items 001–013 visible), the working Item 001/005/007/008/010/014 detail screens (all showing the Export button intact), and the post-crash home screen for Item 013.
- A screen recording (`crash_item013`) captured via Maestro covering the launch → Catalog → tap Item 013 → crash sequence.
- Isolated the fault to Item 013 specifically (adjacent items 012 and 014 both work fine), suggesting a data/indexing bug scoped to that one catalog entry rather than a general list or Export-flow defect.
